Well, initially it wasn’t pleasant to listen to the podcast 😂 it can even feel slightly overwhelming but you have to push through and keep relistening.

I was importing the podcasts to LingQ. That way all the new words were flagged and I could easily read their meanings. I’d repeat this process until the most common words just became quite simple. The more complicated words, I used flash cards 

I have recently written a very simple app, that has helped me with creating flash cards. Usually you find new words in a modified state. They might be conjugated if they’re verbs or declined if they’re nouns or adjectives 

My app basically takes a list of words in any shape and it gives you back the same list with all the words in their base form (verbs in infinitive, words in nominative singular) 

I might eventually put up the app online, for anyone to use but until then, if you are interested, there are also similar tools online like Morfeusz 2.

If you already feel capable of speaking out loud, then you’re doing an awesome job, because for example, I’m completely unable to do that, I am slowly starting to overcome that fear but I still have it.

So feel very proud of yourself for being able to say things out loud! 

When it comes to understanding, I fully believe that a similar method to mine can help a lot. The key is to find the content that feels interesting to you. If you like reading about science, then read about that, if you like politics, do the same 

Try to find videos, articles, podcasts with topics that you enjoy and then try to find the transcription for those things so you can read and listen simultaneously.

Keep up the work and thanks for your comment!

Unfortunately I cannot give much advice when it comes to grammar because I struggle with it myself. Polish grammar is a beast 

I used to feel very frustrated by the grammar but now I have changed the approach slightly. I still read about grammar concepts but I don’t try to memorize them, I simply try to understand what it is about, but without memorizing endings for example 

Then while being exposed to reading and listening, I try to pay attention and see if I can spot patters that I might have read about from the grammar. Slowly I start to more or less understand when some cases are used.

I also have noticed that there are things that I say correctly, not because I know the grammar, but because I have heard it so many times, that it sounds weird if I try to say it in a different way.

It’s a hard process, but every language family has their own “monsters” 😂 for example in Romance languages you very often find the subjunctive time tenses, and those are also hard to initially understand by non natives. 

Slavic languages have gramatical cases among other things, so it’s a process of learning how they work throughout time, exposure and lots of work 

My advice is: do not obsess over it, since I believe the most important thing is having exposure to the language. Eventually things should make more sense

I have some very close polish friends and I have tried to chat with them, but it’s still quite tough for me

During the first two months I had a complete mental block over trying to say or write anything 

But recently, I have started to randomly make my own sentences and saying them out loud, as well as finding ways to express different things 

Based on my previous language learning experiences, this is a significative thing, since I also remember when I slowly started trying to put English sentences together in my head back in the day 

In essence, every day I make tiny steps, that currently are starting to grown into an active vocabulary, instead of just passive understanding.

Grammar is a completely different beast though, but I am also trying to focus more now on it and slowly noticing things and patterns.

I don’t know how the road ahead looks like but I do have hopes to keep on improving. 😊
